Sampled ranking metrics can reverse model orderings relative to full-catalog evaluation, even in expectation; more repetitions do not remove this bias. Thus, HR@10 against 99 negatives measures performance under this benchmark’s candidate protocol, not full-catalog recommendation quality. Preserve the pinned users, candidates, splits and seeds for every comparison. [Krichene and Rendle, 2020](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/).

Recommended uncertainty analysis: retain each model’s binary hit per validation user; bootstrap paired candidate-minus-baseline differences by resampling users within each category, then equally average the four category differences. Report the macro difference, a 95% interval and category results. With 200 users/category, one additional hit changes category HR by 0.005 and macro HR by 0.00125. These intervals describe user-sampling uncertainty conditional on the fixed candidates and trained models; they exclude training randomness, candidate-sampling variability and adaptive selection bias. User-level statistical comparisons are supported by [Cañamares et al., 2020](https://doi.org/10.1007/s10791-020-09371-3); this stratified paired-bootstrap design is a task-specific recommendation.

Repeated checkpoint and hyperparameter selection can overfit validation noise; an ordinary bootstrap interval after selection does not correct that optimism. Predeclare checkpoint cadence, selection and tie-breaking rules; use a small hypothesis-driven search and report checkpoint neighborhoods rather than isolated peaks. Compare component ablations with matched GPU-time allocations and identical evaluation rules, logging all trials and failures within 43,200 GPU-seconds. Keep training seed 42; leave held-out testing to the host. These recommendations follow evidence on [model-selection overfitting](https://jmlr.csail.mit.edu/beta/papers/v11/cawley10a.html) and [recommender baseline reproducibility](https://arxiv.org/abs/1907.06902).
